body.p: The Generate Hash Report for Directory script (generateHash.sh/generateHash.bat, found in the scripts subfolder inside the Oxygen's installation directory) generates a report with a content-aware hash for each file in a directory or ZIP archive. The script does not compare two locations (it only produces the per-file fingerprints that you can later compare.
This script is the command-line equivalent of the Generate Hash Report for Directory tool. See that topic for information about hash calculation, supported content types, and known limitations.

section.title: Arguments for the Generate Hash Report for Directory Script
section.p: On Linux or macOS, use sh generateHash.sh instead of generateHash.bat.

dlentry.dd: Mandatory argument that specifies the target directory or ZIP archive for which the hash report is generated.
Mandatory argument that specifies the path and name of the hash report. The report is XML-formatted. The .xml extension is added if it is not specified.
Optional argument with no value. When present, the script also generates a simplified CSV report with the same path and name as -r and the .csv extension.

Optional argument that specifies a JSON, YAML, or XML configuration file that defines differences to ignore when computing hashes. The file uses the format described in Providing Arguments to Comparison Scripts via a Configuration File. Files that differ only in ignored ways have the same hash.
Optional argument with no value. By default, the script prints only the final result. When present, it also prints each file as the script processes it.

section.note: The dirOrArchivePath, hashReportPath, and diffOptionsFilePath arguments can use relative paths. The script resolves them against the current working directory, including . and .. segments.

section.title: Exit Status and Console Output

dlentry.dd: The script generated the report or reports successfully and printed the path of each generated report.

The script could not generate the report. For example, a mandatory argument is missing, the target or diff options file does not exist, the diff options file is malformed, or the output file's parent directory does not exist. The script prints the reason as an ERROR: line.

section.p: An unrecognized argument does not stop the script. It prints a WARNING line and ignores the argument.
section.codeblock: generateHash.bat -p dirOrArchivePath -r hashReportPath -csb WARNING: Unexpected argument "-csb" ignored. Hash report written to: hashReportPath.xml
section.note: The parent directory of the report file specified by -r must exist. The script does not create it.

section.title: XML Report Format
section.codeblock: <fileHashReport directoryPath="D:/deployments/location-046" diffOptionsFilePath="D:/deployments/diffOptions.json"> <meta name="description" content="File hash report"/> <meta name="author" content="Oxygen XML App Suite"/> <meta name="userName" content="john_doe"/> <meta name="reportTimestamp" content="2026-09-17T10:18:01.3927923"/> <meta name="diffOptions" content="Include files filter:*; ...; Ignore attribute order:true;"/> <dir name="app"> <file name="log.xml" path="app/log.xml" size="1204" modified="2026-09-16T11:30:12.374Z" hash="7e83f485e6ea30e7c7b52614e2f08daaf5c0a6496d5b31091d8a3e162918387f"/> <file name="notes.txt" path="app/notes.txt" size="598" modified="2026-09-16T15:02:10.657Z" hash="1505a90671f30a6c6af075493d77a1b1eb04985ae82716102c42fd8d7c334a64" additionalInfo="hash based on raw file bytes"/> </dir> ...... <file name="results-023.json" path="results-023.json" size="4522" modified="2026-08-16T16:22:19.571Z" hash="1c23bebcbf488bbfa3b6f5f2be6c82a1d490b7a641eda526570ee9ffd0233b4c"/> </fileHashReport>
section.p: File paths are relative to the scanned directory. You can match the same file in reports generated on different machines or from different absolute locations by its path attribute.
For more details about the attributes and elements, and how the hash is computed for each content type, see the Generate Hash Report for Directory Tool topic.

section.title: CSV Report Format
section.p: When you specify -csv, the script writes a flat CSV report alongside the XML report. Use the CSV report in a spreadsheet or SQL-like tool.

ul.li: The report uses semicolons as delimiters. It quotes every field and doubles embedded quotation marks.
The report has one row for each file. It has no rows for directories.
The columns correspond to the attributes of an XML file element. Read the XML report for report metadata, such as the timestamp, user, and diff options.
The script computes each file hash once and uses it in both reports.

section.title: Comparing Reports
section.p: Reports generated by this script use the same format as reports generated by the GUI tool. Generate a report for each location with the same -d diff options file, then compare the reports with XQuery or load the CSV reports into a SQL-capable tool.
For XQuery examples that compare a reference location or check for drift, see Example: Verifying Consistent Deployment Across Multiple Locations.
